title: How Artists Make Money Online in 2026
summary: Explore 9 ways illustrators earn in 2026, from tips and memberships to fonts, brushes, commissions and adopts.
body_markdown:
This is probably one of the most asked questions when you first start out as an artist: how do artists make money? Actually, do they even make money?


And as I say this, I can’t help thinking about how being a ‘broke artist’ has become almost a stereotype. I’m here to tell you otherwise. There’s more evidence than ever that making a living from art isn’t some far-fetched idea.


Whether you’re a beginner or a professional illustrator, there are plenty of ways to earn from your craft. And some of them might surprise you.


But first, let me just give you a sense of how the platform works really. Creators get mainly 3 ways to earn: one-time tips (where supporters buy you a coffee), memberships, and a shop. You can focus on one, or run all side by side.


Now that that’s clear, here are a few interesting ways illustrators are making money with[Buy Me a Coffee](https://www.buymeacoffee.com/) .


---


### One-time tips


### 1. Post tutorials on YouTube, and get tipped on Buy Me a Coffee


You don’t have to sell anything to earn from your art. If you share tutorials on YouTube, you can add Buy Me a Coffee alongside it, so viewers who enjoy your videos have a way to show their support. Even though they post on YouTube,[Mallow](https://buymeacoffee.com/mallows.art.tricks) has been tipped so generously by their audience.


**Here’s how you can do this too:**


- Set up your Buy Me a Coffee page and add a short bio about what you post.
- Embed or link your best tutorial on your page, and add your social links.
- Put your Buy Me a Coffee link in your YouTube video descriptions and pinned comments.


---


### Memberships


### 2. Offer memberships


Membership content can be another source of income if you’d like to offer a combination of things. This could be anything from tutorials, brush kits and sessions to behind-the-scenes videos and exclusive posts. On Buy Me a Coffee, you can set these up as different tiers, each with its own set of offerings.


Take[Derek Domnic D’Souza](https://buymeacoffee.com/derekdsouza/membership) , for example. He offers two membership tiers at $5 and $10 a month. The first includes updated brush sets, art lessons, short tutorials and high-resolution illustrations. The second gives members access to full-length process videos and tutorials on illustration, animation and painting.


**Here’s how you can set this up too:**


- Go to **Memberships** in your dashboard and enable memberships.
- Click **Add a level** to create your first tier.
- Give it a name, set a monthly price and describe what members will get.
- Add the rewards you’re offering, such as exclusive posts, tutorials or downloadable resources.
- Create more levels if you’d like to offer different combinations of perks at different prices.


---


### Shop


Most illustrators on Buy Me a Coffee find their home here, and you guessed it, there’s so many ways you can set up a shop.


### 3. Sell fonts you’ve created


Most illustrators end up creating their own handwritten fonts that they use alongside their artwork. These can have a fanbase of their own. It also doesn’t require you to create anything new, just repurpose a part of your existing work. For inspiration, take a look at[Sketchplanations’ Extras listing](https://buymeacoffee.com/sketchplanator/e/104842) .


If you want to give it a go, here’s how to get started:


- Go to **Shop** in your dashboard and add a new digital product.
- Add the product name, description, preview image, and price.
- Upload the font files using **Upload file** , or choose **Redirect to a URL after purchase** if you’re hosting them elsewhere.


---


### 4. Sell your own art brushes


If you create custom brushes for your digital artwork, you can sell those too. Other artists are always looking for new brushes to experiment with, and the ones you already use in your work could be useful to them. You can add these to your Buy Me a Coffee Shop as digital products.


For example,[this artist](https://buymeacoffee.com/krnpng/extras) has listed their brush sets in their Buy Me a Coffee Shop, with one free set and two others priced at $12 each.


---


### 5. Sell personalised caricatures and comics


If you enjoy drawing people, why not turn that into a personalised product? Custom caricatures and comic-style illustrations make fun gifts, and people are often happy to pay to have themselves, their friends or their pets illustrated.


For example,[illustranged](https://buymeacoffee.com/illustranged/extras/269540) offers custom caricature comics through their Buy Me a Coffee Shop, with listings priced between $39 and $80.


**Here’s how you can do this too:**


- Go to **Shop** in your dashboard and add a new product.
- Add a name, description, sample artwork and price.
- Explain what customers need to send you and what they’ll receive.
- Once someone places an order, get in touch to collect their details and create the artwork.


---


### 6. Sell custom character commissions


If you’d rather draw characters on request than sell ready-made ones, you can take custom commissions too. Buyers get a character designed just for them.


For example,[nuvipi](https://buymeacoffee.com/nuvipionlig/extras/232815) sells custom characters alongside adopts and commissions through their Buy Me a Coffee Shop.


**Here’s how you can do this too:**


- Go to **Shop** in your dashboard and add a new product.
- Add a name, description, sample artwork and price.
- Explain what the buyer needs to send you (references, details, etc.) and what they’ll receive.
- Once someone places an order, get in touch to collect their details and start on the design.


---


### 7. Sell character adopts


If you enjoy creating characters, you can sell those designs too. Some artists create original characters and put them up for sale. Buyers can purchase these designs and use the characters as their own. For inspiration, you can have a look at[Maygebee’s page](https://buymeacoffee.com/maygebee/extras/122077?l=en) .


**Here’s how you can do this too:**


- Go to **Shop** in your dashboard and add a new product.
- Upload your character design, add a description and set a price.
- Include any details about what buyers get and how they can use the design.


---


### 8. Sell VTuber models


VTubers use digital avatars instead of showing their faces on camera. And someone has to design those avatars! If you’re good at character illustration, this is another way to put your skills to use. For inspiration, take a look at[NekoArtDBZ’s page](https://buymeacoffee.com/nekoartdbz/extras/119615) .


---


### 9. Offer one-on-one consultations and creative sessions


If you have experience in a particular area of art or design, you can also offer your time and expertise. This could be a one-on-one consultation, feedback on someone’s work or a longer session to help them work through a creative project.


For example, Truly[Sandra.illus](https://buymeacoffee.com/trulysandra/extras) offers a 30-minute children’s book and graphic design consultation for $50, as well as a three-hour creative session for $150.


You can list these as products in your Buy Me a Coffee Shop, just like the other examples above.


---


### Common mistakes to avoid when selling your art online


- **Not showing enough previews:** If you’re selling digital products, include images that show exactly what buyers will receive.
- **Leaving out important details:** Mention file formats, software compatibility, delivery times and usage rights wherever relevant.
- **Underestimating the time involved:** A commission might look simple, but revisions and customer communication take time too. Account for these when setting your prices.
- **Offering more than you can manage:** If you’re starting memberships, choose rewards you can realistically create and deliver every month.
- **Not updating your listings:** If you change a product, discontinue an offering or update its contents, make sure the listing reflects that.


---


### And, that’s a wrap


If you’ve ever been told you can’t make money from your art, I hope this list proves otherwise. Start small, with whatever you already have. We’d love to see what you make.
